shared_elements: monolithic anthropomorphic pillar/figure with head atop a broad body
low-relief carving on the body surface
animal figures in profile carved on the shaft
arms/hands rendered in low relief converging on the front of the body
curving snake-like or elongated creature on the shaft
stacked registers of motifs down the body
justification: Both are freestanding pillar-like anthropomorphic monoliths whose broad flat bodies bear shallow relief arranged in stacked registers, including profile animals, arms/hands converging on the front, and elongated serpentine creatures running down the shaft — a fairly specific and unusual combination of a figure whose body doubles as a carved panel. The differences lie in the specific motifs: A features prominent concentric discs, a belt-like arc and a face with modelled eyes and nose, whereas B shows a row of crouching quadrupeds along the top, a fringed band, birds and a large downward reptile, with no modelled facial features visible.
